slides.title: Is your glove costing you speed in corners?
slides.sub: Glove tips and cut resistant gloves, explained

slides.title: Your hand is a sensor
slides.body: On a well ridden corner the inside hand is not support. It confirms your lean and gives you a fixed reference point.

slides.title: Bare fabric drags unpredictably
slides.body: Fabric gets wet, freezes and wears through, so the drag changes from lap one to the last. Tips give a hard, smooth, low friction surface.

slides.title: Let your wear pattern decide
slides.body: Fit tips only where your hand actually touches the ice. If only two fingers are scuffed, that is where your tips belong.

slides.title: Fit first, then read the wear
slides.caption: The fingers that touch the ice, four glove fit checks and the signs it is time to replace.

slides.title: Cut resistant does not mean cut proof
slides.body: The glove slows a blade and turns a bad cut into a far less serious one. Wear it and still skate aware of other people's feet.

slides.text: Replace on condition, never on calendar.

slides.title: Sizing, fitting, care and when to replace
